# We need a 6x6 grid with numbers 1..36, each used exactly once.

n = 6
N = n * n  # 36

# Variables: grid[i][j] for 0<=i,j<6, values 1..36
grid = [[z3.Int(f"g_{i}_{j}") for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]

s = z3.Solver()

# Each cell in 1..36
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        s.add(grid[i][j] >= 1)
        s.add(grid[i][j] <= N)

# All distinct
s.add(z3.Distinct([grid[i][j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n)]))

# Row sums and col sums
row_sums = [z3.Int(f"r_{i}") for i in range(n)]
col_sums = [z3.Int(f"c_{j}") for j in range(n)]
for i in range(n):
    s.add(row_sums[i] == z3.Sum([grid[i][j] for j in range(n)]))
for j in range(n):
    s.add(col_sums[j] == z3.Sum([grid[i][j] for i in range(n)]))

# Diagonals
diag1 = z3.Int("d1")
diag2 = z3.Int("d2")
s.add(diag1 == z3.Sum([grid[i][i] for i in range(n)]))
s.add(diag2 == z3.Sum([grid[i][n-1-i] for i in range(n)]))

# All 14 sums must be distinct
all_sums = row_sums + col_sums + [diag1, diag2]
s.add(z3.Distinct(all_sums))

# They must be 14 consecutive integers: max - min = 13
# We can add constraints: there exists s such that all sums are in {s, s+1, ..., s+13}
# Equivalent: max(sums) - min(sums) == 13 AND all sums distinct (already ensured)

min_sum = z3.Int("min_sum")
max_sum = z3.Int("max_sum")

s.add(min_sum == z3.Min(*all_sums))
s.add(max_sum == z3.Max(*all_sums))
s.add(max_sum - min_sum == 13)
